result.resolution: This keyboard showed no 8 or 16 ms reporting schedule in this test.

outcome.title: The fault moved with the switch.
evidence: E: no extra key-downs in 90 presses, so a rate above 3.4% would very likely have shown
G: 18 of 90 presses sent an extra key-down (a rate of at least 13%)
outcome.diagnosis: The E switch now sits in the G socket, and the fault appeared there. The switch is the most likely cause. The E socket and the PCB behaved normally with a known-good switch.
next: Blow out the switch that came from E, now in the G socket, with G held down, or work contact cleaner into it while pressing G many times. Then test G again.
Replace the switch that came from E, now in the G socket, with a switch of the same model. Then test G again.

result.resolution: This keyboard showed no 8 or 16 ms reporting schedule in this test.

outcome.title: The fault stayed on E.
evidence: E: 18 of 90 presses sent an extra key-down (a rate of at least 13%)
G: no extra key-downs in 90 presses, so a rate above 3.4% would very likely have shown
outcome.diagnosis: A known-good switch in the E socket shows the same fault. The socket, the solder joints under it, or the matrix trace is the most likely cause. The original switch is probably fine.
next: Inspect the E socket for a loose pin and the joints under it for a crack. Reflowing the socket pins is a small job. If the board is under warranty, this result is what the vendor needs.
